```yaml
name: PR Status Labeler

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [PR Auto-Labeler]
    types: [completed]

jobs:
  capture-pr-data:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v2

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v2
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install requests

      - name: Capture PR data
        id: capture_pr_data
        run: |
          echo "::set-output name=pr_number::$(jq -r '.pull_request.number' $GITHUB_EVENT_PATH)"
          echo "::set-output name=pr_repo::$(jq -r '.pull_request.head.repo.full_name' $GITHUB_EVENT_PATH)"

  pr-status-labeler:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: capture-pr-data
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v2

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v2
        with:
          python-version: '3.x'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install requests

      - name: Get PR data
        run: |
          pr_number=${{ needs.capture-pr-data.outputs.pr_number }}
          pr_repo=${{ needs.capture-pr-data.outputs.pr_repo }}

      - name: Label PR
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          curl -X POST \
            https://api.github.com/repos/${{ github.repository }}/issues/${{ pr_number }}/labels \
            -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -d '["label1", "label2"]'
```

This workflow captures the necessary data from the `PR Auto-Labeler` workflow and then labels the pull request using the captured data. It ensures that the PR status labeler has the necessary permissions to label PRs, even from forks, by using the `workflow_run` trigger.
